items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: That's the last recording that J. J. Johnson made with the band.

ctx.x: Then he joined Basie. That's when he made the record, 'The King.'

Which he says, his is mine. I didn't know it was mine till after, because they had been recording for about 3 hours and I walked in with a sock cymbal and I said, 'Shadow, get up for a minute. Let me have this band for a minute. Fellows, it goes like this.' That's the last recording that J. J. Johnson made with the band.
J. J. Johnson was with Basie?

items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Illinois Jacquet. Jo Jones, the drummer – the Basie Jo Jones, not the Philly Joe Jones.

ctx.x: Who were some of your good friends in the Basie band when you were with them? Did you have anyone you were particularly close to?
Joe Newman. Dickie Wells and I would hang out together. Illinois Jacquet. Jo Jones, the drummer – the Basie Jo Jones, not the Philly Joe Jones.
